tagline: Out of the tunnel and on through the oak hills.
intro: Highway 24 comes out of the east portal of the Caldecott Tunnel into Contra Costa County, with the Berkeley Hills now between it and Oakland. The freeway runs east through wooded hillsides and suburbs, Orinda and then Lafayette, crosses the Mokelumne Aqueduct and ends at Interstate 680 just inside Walnut Creek. For most of the way BART trains run down the median.

People talked of a tunnel here as early as 1860. A private bore in 1871 got about 200 feet into the hill before it struck water and washed out. The first two bores of the Caldecott opened in 1937, and the fourth in 2013.

moments.title: Caldecott Tunnel
moments.text: Named for Thomas Caldecott, once mayor of Berkeley. The two oldest bores, from 1937, carry the eastbound lanes out to this side of the hills.

moments.title: Orinda
moments.text: Named in 1876 by a sheriff whose wife loved the poems of Katherine Philips, the Matchless Orinda. It filled in as a year-round town after the tunnel opened.

moments.title: Lafayette
moments.text: Elam Brown came from Missouri in 1846, bought the Acalanes rancho and built a mill. Residents still say the town's name at least three different ways.
